===Etymology===
[[File:Russian_Imperial_Family_1913.jpg|thumb|The Russian Imperial family in 1913]]

{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} {{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|famylye}}, from {{der|en|la|familia||a household}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hīred}}. {{dbt|en|familia}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q8436}} A group of people who are closely related to one another (by [[blood]], [[marriage]] or [[adoption]]); [[kin]]; in particular, a set of parents and their children; an [[immediate family]].
#: {{ux|en|Our '''family''' lives in town.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|volume=III|chapter=XI|page=200|passage=To Jane, he could be only a man whose proposals she had refused, and whose merit she had undervalued; but to her own more extensive information, he was the person, to whom the whole '''family''' were indebted for the first of benefits, and whom she regarded herself with an interest, if not quite so tender, at least as reasonable and just, as what Jane felt for Bingley.}}
#* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=Prologue|passage=Such a [[scandal]] as the prosecution of a [[brother]] for forgery—with a verdict of guilty—is a most truly horrible, deplorable, fatal thing. It takes the respectability out of a '''family''' perhaps at a critical [[moment]], when the '''family''' is just assuming the robes of respectability:{{...}}it is a black spot which all the soaps ever advertised could never wash off.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=Towards the end of poverty| date=2013-06-01| volume=407| issue=8838| page=11| magazine=w:The Economist| url=http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21578665-nearly-1-billion-people-have-been-taken-out-extreme-poverty-20-years-world-should-aim| passage=America’s poverty line is $63 a day for a '''family''' of four. In the richer parts of the emerging world $4 a day is the poverty barrier. But poverty’s scourge is fiercest below $1.25 ([&hellip;]): people below that level live lives that are poor, nasty, brutish and short.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/HjLZ6|archivedate=2024-09-05}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Kat Kinsman|title=Something borrowed: Wedding traditions from around the world|magazine=w:CNN|url=https://www.cnn.com/2013/08/30/living/matrimony-global-traditions|date=2013-08-30|passage=Both brides and grooms in native Hawaiian tradition wear flower garlands as a physical manifestation of their love for one another, and to some, the twining of the stems is reflective of two '''families''' now becoming one. A more tourist-friendly version established in the past couple of decades involves winding the leis around the couple’s hands to bind them together.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|date=May 6 2018|actor=w:John Oliver|title=w:Last Week Tonight with John Oliver|season= 5|number=10| episode=Rudy Giuliani| network=HBO|text= They’re both New Yorkers coasting on their reputations, they’ve both had three marriages, neither of them can shut up when in front of a camera, and perhaps most importantly, they both want to fuck Ivanka, which-which is weird for Trump because Ivanka is in his '''family''', and it’s weird for Giuliani because she isn’t.}}
# An [[extended family]]: a group of people who are related to one another by blood or marriage.
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1915|author=William T. Groves|title=A History and Genealogy of the Groves '''Family''' in America}}
# A [[nuclear family]]: a mother and father who are married and cohabiting and their child or children.
#: {{ux|en|The cultural struggle is for the survival of '''family''' values against all manner of atheistic amorality.}}
#: {{ux|en|We must preserve the '''family''' unit if we want to save civilisation!}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Members of one's family collectively.
#: {{ux|en|I have a lot of '''family''' in Australia.}}
#: {{ux|en|He has a sister, but no other '''family'''.}}
# A (close-knit) [[group]] of [[people]] related by [[blood]], friendship, [[marriage]], law, or custom, especially if they live or work together.
#: {{ux|en|crime '''family''''', ''Mafia '''family'''}}<!--move to its own sense if needed, but for now, I'll account for this usage by this usex here-->
#: {{ux|en|This is my fraternity '''family''' at the university.}}
#: {{ux|en|Our company is one big happy '''family'''.}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable|gay slang}} The [[gay]] [[community]].
##* {{quote-journal|en|author=Gloria Godqueen|work=w:Bay Area Reporter|volume=12|number=28|date=July 15, 1982|title=What's in a card|page=7|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/BAR_19820715/page/n6/mode/1up|passage={{...}}This is not your hallmark im Ames, Iowa. And there is “'''family'''” working there . . . no radar like gaydar, I always say.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[lineage|Lineage]], especially honorable or [[noble]] lineage.
#* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|text=Indeed, he married her for love. A whisper still goes about that she had not even ''''family''''; howbeit, Sir Leicester had so much '''family''' that perhaps he had enough and could dispense with any more.|2}}
# Any [[group]] or aggregation of [[things]] classed together as [[kindred]] or related from possessing in [[common]] [[characteristics]] which distinguish them from other things of the same [[order]].
#: {{ux|en|Doliracetam is a drug from the racetam '''family'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Scott Mueller; Mark Edward Soper|title=Upgrading and Repairing PCs: Technician's Portable Reference|publisher=Que Publishing|isbn=9780789724540|page=115|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=7M5qK8Y-Ip4C&q=%22connector%22&dq=%22connector%22&hl=&cd=53&source=gbs_api|text=Because SCSI is actually a '''family''' of standards, each with its own cable and connector, matching cables and connectors to the appropriate SCSI “family member” is important.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Gary Shelly; Jennifer Campbell; Ollie Rivers|title=Microsoft Expression Web 3: Complete|page=262|passage=When creating a font '''family''', first decide whether to use all serif or all sans-serif fonts, then choose two or three fonts of that type {{...}}}}
## {{senseid|en|taxonomy}} {{lb|en|biology|taxonomy}} A [[category]] in the [[classification]] of [[organism]]s, ranking below [[order]] and above [[genus]]; a [[taxon]] at that rank.
##: {{syn|en|familia}}
##: {{ux|en|Magnolias belong to the '''family''' Magnoliaceae.}}
##* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=4|text=The closest affinities of the Jubulaceae are with the Lejeuneaceae. The two '''families''' share in common: ''a'' elaters usually 1-spiral, trumpet-shaped and fixed to the capsule valves, distally{{nb...}}.}}
## {{lb|en|set theory|countable}} A collection of [[set]]s, especially of [[subset]]s of a given set.
##: {{ux|en|Let <math>\mathcal F</math> be a '''family''' of subsets over <math>S</math>.}}
## {{lb|en|music}} A group of instruments having the same basic method of tone production.
##: {{ux|en|the brass '''family''';&emsp; the violin '''family'''}}
## {{lb|en|linguistics}} A group of languages believed to have [[descended]] from the same [[ancestral]] language.
##: {{syn|en|language family}}
##: {{coi|en|the Indo-European '''family'''}}
##: {{coi|en|the Afroasiatic '''family'''}}
#* {{RQ:Withycombe Christian Names|edition=1st|chapter=Introduction|page=xi|passage=Of the great Indo-European '''family''' of languages the general principal was also that of one name for each individual{{...|, the majority of names being compounded of two elements chosen from a stock of special name-words.}}}}

====Usage notes====
{{tea room|en|m=April|y=2025}}
* In some dialects, for a family of humans (relatives, parents, children, etc), [[w:notional agreement|notional agreement]] is the norm and [[w:formal agreement|formal agreement]] is uncommon. Thus ''the family '''are''' coming for a holiday dinner'' rather than ''the family '''is''' coming for a holiday dinner''.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|-}}

# Suitable for children and adults.
#: {{ux|en|It's not good for a date, it's a '''family''' restaurant.}}
#: {{ux|en|Some animated movies are not just for kids, they are '''family''' movies.}}
